examples.en: I put gauze on the wound and secured it with tape.

examples.ko: 약국에서 멸균 거즈를 한 상자 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a box of sterile gauze at the pharmacy.
The gauze got soaked with blood, so I replaced it.

examples.ko: 아기 얼굴은 거즈 수건으로 닦아 주세요.
examples.en: Please wipe the baby's face with a gauze towel.
The nurse pressed it with gauze to stop the bleeding.

examples.ko: 거즈 한 장만 더 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you give me one more piece of gauze?

explain: 거즈는 영어 gauze에서 온 말이라 병원과 약국에서 그대로 써요. 작은 상처에 붙이는 반창고는 '밴드'라고 하는 사람이 많아요. 아기 용품에서는 부드러운 천을 '거즈 손수건'처럼 불러요.

phrases.en: Use sterile gauze on the wound.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세균이 없게 만든 깨끗한 거즈를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gauze made germ-free and clean.

phrases.en: I put on medicine and then stuck on gauze.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상처 위에 덮을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The usual phrase for covering a wound.

phrases.en: I bought a gauze handkerchief for the baby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원 용품이 아니라 부드러운 아기 용품에도 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for soft baby goods, not only medical supplies.

explain_en: 거즈 comes from the English word gauze and is used as is in hospitals and pharmacies. Many people call small adhesive bandages '밴드'. In baby goods, soft cloth is named like '거즈 손수건'.

en: to examine; to do a checkup

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 환자의 폐를 꼼꼼하게 검진했어요.
examples.en: The doctor examined the patient's lungs carefully.
I went to the pediatrician to have the baby examined.

examples.ko: 오늘 검진한 결과는 다음 주에 나와요.
examples.en: The results of today's checkup will come out next week.

examples.ko: 치아를 검진하고 나서 치료 계획을 세웠어요.
examples.en: After the dental checkup, we made a treatment plan.
The company gives employees free checkups.

examples.ko: 검진하러 갈 때는 아침을 먹지 말고 가세요.
examples.en: When you go for a checkup, don't eat breakfast.

explain: '검진하다'는 아픈 곳이 없어도 건강한지 정기적으로 살펴볼 때 써요. 아픈 곳이 있어서 의사를 만나는 '진찰받다', '진료받다'와 달라요. 보통 '건강검진을 받다'라고 말하고, '검진하다'는 의사나 병원이 주어일 때 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 의사 선생님이 아이를 꼼꼼하게 검진해 주셨어요.
phrases.en: The doctor examined the child carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: '검진하다'에 '-아/어 주다'를 붙이면 의사가 환자를 위해 살펴 준다는 느낌이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아/어 주다 gives the sense that the doctor examines someone for their benefit.

phrases.en: As a result of the checkup, there was no problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 검진을 마친 뒤 결과를 말할 때 쓰는 연결 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A linking phrase used when reporting the outcome after an examination.
phrases.en_equiv: as a result of the checkup

phrases.en: The hospital is examining patients one by one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 검진이 지금 진행되는 중임을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the examination is happening right now.

explain_en: '검진하다' is for routine checks on whether you are healthy, even with no symptoms. It differs from '진찰받다' or '진료받다', which means seeing a doctor for a problem. Patients usually say '건강검진을 받다', and '검진하다' fits better when the doctor or hospital is the subject.

examples.en: I have to fast from the night before the test.

examples.ko: 수술을 앞두고 열두 시간째 금식하고 있어요.
examples.en: I've been fasting for twelve hours before the surgery.

examples.ko: 아침에 피를 뽑는다고 해서 어제 저녁부터 금식했어요.
examples.en: They said they'd draw blood in the morning, so I fasted from last evening.

examples.ko: 금식하는 동안 물은 마셔도 되는지 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I asked whether I could drink water while fasting.

examples.ko: 금식하기 전에 의사 선생님 설명을 잘 들으세요.
examples.en: Listen carefully to the doctor's instructions before you fast.
My grandmother fasts on her prayer days.

explain: 병원에서 검사나 수술 전에 '내일 아침까지 금식하세요'라고 많이 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '금식 중이에요'처럼 명사 '금식'도 써요. 다이어트로 안 먹을 때는 '굶다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I'm fasting right now because of a test.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '금식'을 써서 지금 아무것도 안 먹는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 금식 to say you are in a no-eating state right now.

phrases.en: Please don't eat anything until tomorrow morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 의사나 간호사가 환자에게 안내할 때 자주 쓰는 높임 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite instruction commonly given by doctors and nurses to patients.

phrases.en: You don't have to fast for this test.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 먹어도 된다고 알려 줄 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell someone they are allowed to eat and fasting isn't required.

explain_en: At hospitals you often hear 내일 아침까지 금식하세요 before a test or surgery. The noun 금식 also works, as in 금식 중이에요. For skipping meals to diet, use 굶다 instead.

examples.ko: 할머니가 구멍 난 양말을 깁고 계세요.
examples.en: Grandmother is mending the socks with holes.
My pants tore, so I am patching them myself.
I just threw the clothes away without mending them.

examples.ko: 찢어진 곳을 깁기만 하면 아직 입을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you just mend the torn spot, you can still wear it.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 낡은 옷을 깁고 또 입었어요.
examples.en: In the old days people patched worn clothes and wore them again.

examples.ko: 엄마는 바늘로 가방을 깁는 걸 잘하세요.
examples.en: My mom is good at mending bags with a needle.

explain: '깁다'는 ㅂ 불규칙이라 '기워요', '기웠어요', '기운'으로 바뀌어요. 천이나 옷의 찢어진 곳을 바늘로 고칠 때 쓰고, 단추를 다는 것은 '달다'예요. '꿰매다'와 바꿔 써도 거의 같아요.

phrases.en: I mend torn clothes myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: ㅂ 불규칙 활용인 해요체로, 일상 대화에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite ending with the ㅂ irregular change, used in daily talk.

phrases.en: My grandmother is wearing mended clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깁다'가 명사를 꾸미는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past modifier form of 깁다, describing a noun.

phrases.en: I sewed up the torn pants with a needle.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깁다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로, 바늘과 실로 고칠 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 깁다, used for fixing with needle and thread.

explain_en: 깁다 is a ㅂ-irregular verb, so it becomes '기워요', '기웠어요' and '기운'. It is for fixing a torn spot in cloth with needle and thread. Attaching a button is '달다'. You can swap in '꿰매다' with almost no change.

examples.en: I hurt my leg and got a cast.
When do you take the cast off?
It is inconvenient to shower because of the cast.
I wrote my name on my friend's cast.
My friends drew pictures on the cast.
The cast feels very stuffy.

explain: 독일어 'Gips'에서 온 말이고, 병원에서는 '석고 붕대'라고도 해요. '깁스를 하다', '깁스를 풀다'처럼 말하고, 다친 팔이나 다리를 감싸면 '깁스한 다리'가 돼요.

phrases.en: I broke my arm, so I got a cast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다친 곳에 깁스를 하는 가장 기본적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to say you got a cast on an injury.

phrases.en: I'm getting my cast off next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다 나아서 깁스를 뗄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the cast is removed after healing.

phrases.en: My leg in a cast keeps itching.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깁스하다'를 명사 앞에 붙여 다친 부위를 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Puts 'wear a cast' before a noun to describe the injured body part.

explain_en: The word comes from the German 'Gips', and in hospitals it is also called 석고 붕대. You say '깁스를 하다' (get a cast) and '깁스를 풀다' (take it off), and a leg in a cast is '깁스한 다리'.

examples.en: I had a bad body ache and groaned all night.

examples.ko: 문제가 안 풀려서 혼자 끙끙대고 있어요.
examples.en: I can't solve the problem, so I'm struggling over it alone.

examples.ko: 고민만 하며 끙끙대지 말고 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't just worry and suffer in silence. Tell me.
The baby seemed to have a fever and slept while whimpering.

examples.ko: 무거운 짐을 들고 끙끙대는 할머니를 도와드렸어요.
examples.en: I helped the grandmother who was struggling with her heavy bags.
You don't need to struggle alone. I'll help you.

explain: 아파서 앓는 소리를 낼 때와 해결하기 어려운 일로 혼자 괴로워할 때 둘 다 써요. '끙끙 앓다'는 자주 쓰는 짝이에요. '끙끙거리다'와 거의 같게 쓰이고, 힘들게 애쓰는 모습이 보이는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I had a fever last night and moaned in pain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아파서 앓는 소리를 낼 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for moaning in sickness.

phrases.en: I struggled with my homework until late at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로 오래 힘들게 애쓴 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past form for struggling hard over something for a long time.

phrases.example: 혼자 끙끙대지 말고 저한테 말해 주세요.
phrases.en: Don't struggle alone; tell me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혼자 고민하는 사람에게 도움을 청하라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said to someone worrying alone, urging them to ask for help.

explain_en: It is used both for making groaning sounds when you are in pain and for suffering alone over a difficult problem. '끙끙 앓다' is a common pairing. It is used almost the same way as '끙끙거리다' and shows someone struggling hard.

examples.en: Your posture looks good when your spine is straight.

examples.ko: 사람의 등뼈는 여러 개의 뼈로 이루어져 있어요.
examples.en: A human spine is made up of many bones.
I fell and almost hurt my spine.
I made pork bone soup with pork backbone.
The doctor checked the shape of my spine with an X-ray.
The backbone of a fish has many small bones.

explain: '척추'는 의학이나 설명할 때 많이 쓰고, '등뼈'는 일상에서 더 쉽게 말하는 표현이에요. 요리에서는 돼지 등뼈로 끓이는 감자탕처럼 재료 이름으로도 나와요.

phrases.en: Straighten your spine when you sit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자세를 바르게 하라고 할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell someone to correct their posture.

phrases.example: 오래 앉아 있으면 척추에 안 좋아요.
phrases.en: Sitting for a long time is bad for your spine.
phrases.nuance_ko: '등뼈'와 같은 뼈를 가리키지만 설명이나 병원에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the same bone as 등뼈 but is used more in explanations and at hospitals.

phrases.en: I made gamjatang with pork spine bones.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리에서 고기 재료 이름으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as the name of a meat ingredient in cooking.

explain_en: '척추' is common in medical or explanatory contexts, while '등뼈' is the plainer everyday word. In cooking it also appears as an ingredient, as in 감자탕 made with pork backbone.

examples.ko: 배가 너무 아파서 맹장 검사를 받았어요.
examples.en: My stomach hurt so much that I had an appendix check.
I had an appendix operation and stayed a week in the hospital.
It's dangerous if the appendix bursts.
My younger sibling got appendicitis.

examples.ko: 오른쪽 아랫배가 아프면 맹장일 수 있어요.
examples.en: If your lower right belly hurts, it could be the appendix.
Where in the body is the appendix?

explain: 병원에서는 '충수'라고도 하지만 일상에서는 '맹장'이라고 해요. 염증이 생긴 병은 보통 '맹장염'이라고 하고, 수술은 '맹장 수술'이라고 불러요.

phrases.en: I rushed to the hospital because of appendicitis.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맹장에 염증이 생긴 병을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the illness where the appendix becomes inflamed.

phrases.en: My younger sibling had an appendix operation yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원 이야기에서 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation in talk about hospitals.

phrases.example: 늦게 가면 맹장이 터질 수도 있어요.
phrases.en: If you go late, your appendix could burst.
phrases.nuance_ko: 염증이 심해서 맹장이 터지는 위험한 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the dangerous case where an inflamed appendix bursts.

explain_en: In medical settings it can be called 충수, but in daily life people say 맹장. The inflamed condition is usually 맹장염, and the operation is called 맹장 수술.

examples.en: That singer has a tattoo on his arm.
Removing a tattoo takes a long time.

examples.ko: 어떤 대중목욕탕은 문신이 있는 사람은 못 들어가요.
examples.en: Some public baths don't let in people with tattoos.

examples.ko: 아이 이름을 문신으로 새긴 아빠를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a dad who had his child's name tattooed.
A tattoo sticker comes off after a few days.

examples.ko: 저는 아프다고 해서 문신은 안 하기로 했어요.
examples.en: I heard it hurts, so I decided not to get a tattoo.

explain: '문신을 하다', '문신을 새기다'처럼 써요. 한국에서는 목욕탕, 수영장, 헬스장 중에 문신이 있으면 입장을 막는 곳이 있어서 알아 두면 좋아요. 지워지는 가짜 문신은 '타투 스티커'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: My friend got a tattoo on the shoulder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔하게 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing.

phrases.en: I got a star-shaped tattoo on my back.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하다'보다 몸에 새긴다는 느낌이 강해서 글에서 잘 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: More vivid than '하다', suggesting the design is engraved on the body; often seen in writing.

phrases.en: I couldn't enter the bathhouse because of my tattoo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국에서 문신이 입장 제한 이유가 될 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a tattoo is the reason for being refused entry in Korea.

explain_en: It is used as '문신을 하다' or '문신을 새기다'. In Korea some bathhouses, pools, and gyms refuse entry to people with tattoos, which is good to know. A removable fake one is called a '타투 스티커'.

examples.en: We keep medicine at home, so I took a headache pill.
Pack some basic medicine when you travel.
You can buy basic medicines at a convenience store.
I keep cold medicine and a digestive aid ready as basic medicine.

examples.ko: 상비약 상자를 정리하니 유통기한이 지난 약이 많았어요.
examples.en: When I tidied the medicine box, many pills were past their expiry date.

examples.ko: 상비약은 아이 손이 닿지 않는 곳에 두세요.
examples.en: Keep basic medicine out of children's reach.

explain: 열이나 두통, 소화불량처럼 갑자기 필요할 때를 위해 집이나 가방에 늘 두는 약이에요. 병원에서 받은 처방약이 아니라 약국이나 편의점에서 쉽게 사는 약을 말해요. '구급약'과 비슷하게 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.example: 밤에 머리가 아파서 편의점 상비약을 샀어요.
phrases.en: My head hurt at night, so I bought over-the-counter medicine at a convenience store.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편의점에서 살 수 있는 약을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for medicine you can buy at a convenience store.

phrases.en: It's convenient to keep first-aid medicine at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 준비해 둔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means having them prepared in advance.

phrases.en: I carry first-aid medicine in my bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻이고, 갑자기 다쳤을 때 쓰는 약이라는 느낌이 더 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, with more of a sense of medicine for sudden injuries.

explain_en: It is medicine you always keep at home or in a bag for sudden needs, like fever, headache or indigestion. It refers to easy over-the-counter medicine, not prescriptions from a hospital. It is sometimes used much like '구급약'.

examples.en: Today I tried putting on brown eye shadow.
This eye shadow sparkles nicely around the eyes.
My eye shadow smeared and came off because of sweat.
I got sparkly eye shadow as a gift from a friend.

examples.ko: 아이섀도 색깔을 고르는 게 너무 어려워요.
examples.en: Choosing an eye shadow color is so hard.
Which eye shadow color suits me?

explain: 눈 화장에 쓰는 화장품이고, 외래어 표기법에 따라 '아이쉐도'가 아니라 '아이섀도'라고 써요. 화장품 가게에서는 '아이라이너', '마스카라'와 함께 자주 나와요. 바르다, 칠하다, 하다와 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I applied eye shadow on my eyelids.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화장품을 피부에 얹을 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb for putting makeup on skin.

phrases.en: I put on light pink eye shadow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색을 입힌다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives a sense of coloring the eyelid.

phrases.en: I bought eye shadow and mascara together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈 화장품을 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when naming eye makeup items together.

explain_en: This is makeup for the eyelids, and the standard spelling is '아이섀도', not '아이쉐도'. It often appears together with '아이라이너' (eyeliner) and '마스카라' (mascara) at cosmetics shops. It goes with verbs like 바르다, 칠하다 and 하다.

examples.en: The paramedic gave artificial respiration to the person who collapsed.
I learned how to do artificial respiration in class.

examples.ko: 인공호흡은 응급 상황에서 배워 두면 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Artificial respiration is helpful to learn for emergencies.
I saw a practice dummy for artificial respiration at the pool.
To save the child, he breathed air in with artificial respiration.
If artificial respiration is needed, call 119 first.

explain: '인공호흡'은 숨을 쉬지 못하는 사람에게 입으로 숨을 불어넣는 응급 처치예요. 심장이 멈춘 경우에는 가슴을 누르는 '심폐소생술'과 함께 배워요. '인공호흡을 하다'로 말하고, 병원에서 기계로 숨 쉬게 하는 건 '인공호흡기'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I learned rescue breathing and CPR together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인공호흡과 가슴을 누르는 일을 합친 응급 처치 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name for emergency care that combines rescue breaths and chest compressions.

phrases.en: Please tell me how to do rescue breathing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방법을 묻거나 배울 때 '방법'과 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 방법 when asking about or learning the steps.

phrases.en: The patient was put on a ventilator.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 기계로 숨 쉬게 하는 장치를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the machine that helps a patient breathe in a hospital.

explain_en: 인공호흡 is the emergency first-aid method of blowing air into the mouth of someone who is not breathing. When the heart stops, it is taught together with chest compressions, called 심폐소생술. The verb is 인공호흡을 하다, and the hospital machine that breathes for a patient is 인공호흡기.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 청진기로 가슴 소리를 들었어요.
examples.en: The doctor listened to my chest with a stethoscope.
A nurse with a stethoscope around her neck walked by.

examples.ko: 아이가 장난감 청진기를 귀에 대 봤어요.
examples.en: The child put a toy stethoscope to their ear.
The stethoscope felt cold and surprised me.
Medical students start by learning how to use a stethoscope.
I heard the stethoscope broke, so they bought a new one.

explain: 병원 장면에서 자주 나오는 단어예요. '청진기를 대다'처럼 쓰고, 이렇게 소리를 들으며 몸을 살피는 일은 '진찰'과 같이 연결해서 기억하면 쉬워요.

phrases.en: The doctor put the stethoscope on my chest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진찰하는 동작을 말할 때 가장 기본적으로 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic collocation for the action of examining.

phrases.en: The doctor came walking with a stethoscope around his neck.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 의사나 간호사의 모습을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe how doctors or nurses look at the hospital.
phrases.en_equiv: to wear a stethoscope around the neck

phrases.en: The doctor examined me with a stethoscope and gave me medicine.
phrases.nuance_ko: '진찰'과 함께 도구와 행동을 한 문장에 묶어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links the tool and the action 'examine' in one sentence.

explain_en: This word often appears in hospital scenes. It is used like '청진기를 대다' (to place a stethoscope), and it's easier to remember by linking it with '진찰' (medical examination).

examples.en: My shoulder hurt, so I put on a pain patch.

examples.ko: 파스는 약국에서 쉽게 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can easily buy pain patches at a pharmacy.

examples.ko: 운동한 뒤에 다리에 파스를 붙이고 잤어요.
examples.en: After exercising, I put a patch on my leg and slept.
There is a smell of pain patches in Grandma's room.

examples.ko: 파스를 오래 붙이면 피부가 가려울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you wear a patch too long, your skin can get itchy.

examples.ko: 허리에 붙이는 파스 한 봉지를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a pack of patches to put on my back.

explain: 근육이 아플 때 피부에 붙이는 얇은 약이에요. 한국에서는 파스가 아주 흔해서 어른들이 자주 붙여요. 붙이는 약은 '붙이다'를 쓰고, 바르는 약은 '바르다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Please give me one pain patch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얇은 파스를 셀 때는 '장'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Thin patches are counted with 장.

phrases.en: Take off the patch before you sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 붙인 파스를 몸에서 뗄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when removing a patch you put on.

phrases.en: I went to the pharmacy to buy a pain patch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약국에서 파스를 살 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for buying a patch at a pharmacy.

explain_en: A thin medicated patch stuck on the skin for muscle pain. They are very common in Korea, especially among older adults. You '붙이다' a patch, but '바르다' a cream.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 넘어져서 무릎에 흉터가 생겼어요.
examples.en: I fell as a child and got a scar on my knee.
I put on makeup to cover the scar on my face.
The surgery scar is almost invisible.

examples.ko: 이 흉터는 어릴 때 자전거 사고로 생겼어요.
examples.en: I got this scar from a bike accident when I was young.
The wound healed, but the scar remained.
Apply ointment so it doesn't leave a scar.

explain: '상처'는 다친 곳 자체이고, 다 나은 뒤에 남은 자국이 '흉터'예요. '흉터가 생기다', '흉터가 남다'로 자주 말해요. 마음의 아픔에는 '흉터'보다 '상처'를 써요.

phrases.en: I fell and got a scar on my leg.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상처가 나은 뒤 자국이 새로 생겼을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a mark newly forms after a wound heals.

phrases.en: A small scar remained after the surgery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다 나았는데도 자국이 계속 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a mark stays even after healing.

phrases.en: I bought a cream that gets rid of scars.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자국을 지우거나 옅게 하려는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for trying to remove or fade a scar.

explain_en: '상처' is the injury itself; the mark left after it heals is '흉터'. People say '흉터가 생기다' or '흉터가 남다'. For emotional pain use '상처', not '흉터'.
